description: Common type definitions for cryptographic signatures attached to records, per the ATProtocol Attestation Specification. Each signature's `$type` says what it attests.

list.description: Reusable array of cryptographic signatures on a record. Each entry's `$type` says what it attests. The union is open: other applications may define their own signature types, and consumers ignore types they do not recognize.

inline.description: Inline attestation signature embedded directly in a record. Conforms to the ATProtocol Attestation Specification: the signed input is the 36-byte CIDv1 (dag-cbor + SHA-256) of the record with the `signatures` field removed and a temporary `$sig` metadata object (containing `$type`, `key` and the housing repository DID) inserted before canonical DAG-CBOR encoding. ECDSA with the low-S variant per BIP-0062 is required; the curve (P-256 or K-256) is determined by the multicodec prefix of the verification method's `publicKeyMultibase`.

signature.description: ECDSA signature bytes (raw r,s) over the 36-byte CID of the record. Low-S variant per BIP-0062 is mandatory.

key.description: Full DID verification method reference (format: did:{method}:{identifier}#{fragment}). Identifies the signer and the specific key used; the key's multicodec prefix determines the signing curve.

createdVia.description: Inline signature by the application that wrote this version of the record. It does not mean the application endorses the content. A record carries at most one `#createdVia` signature. Signed exactly like `#inline`: `$sig` is this signature entry without its `signature` field (so `$type` and `key`), plus `repository`, the DID of the repository that holds the record.

signature.description: ECDSA signature bytes (raw r,s) over the 36-byte CID of the record. Low-S variant per BIP-0062 is mandatory.

key.description: DID verification method of the application's signing key (format: did:{method}:{identifier}#{fragment}), e.g. a key in the application's did:web document. The DID identifies the application; the key's multicodec prefix determines the signing curve.
